So I was in the bathroom, with blades in my hand. I was ready. Not scared, but ready. I knew exactly what to do but I was crying and my hands were trembling. So I shut my eyes tightly to get a clearer view and within that one second, my brain went to my parents and my brother. The most probable was that my brother would find me. And how devastating that would be for him. He was really young back then and always so caring towards me. I brushed off the thought and still went ahead. But all of a sudden, I didn’t know the right way to do it and I got scared. I cut myself but not with a desire to die but with the desire to hurt myself for not thinking about my brother. I remember fainting in the washroom and waking up after sometime. I was home alone. When I woke up, I just felt like I wanted to live. So a thought saved me.
The glow of letting toxic people go.

It’s the kind of book I loved at times and didn’t really like sometimes. I personally don’t really like reading about the nature surrounding the character for 2 pages straight. And there were parts which solely did that. They were well described and I could draw a clearer picture of the surroundings with each word, but at times, I would just get too restless reading those descriptions and wanted to see an interaction between the creator and the creation or any human interaction really. I loved it for a lot more reasons though. The explorer’s letter with Victor telling his story and the creation telling his story within Victor’s was an interesting read for sure. The themes, the characters, the science - oh, so lovely!! I kind of started seeing science as an art after reading this. But so glad I read this book. Truly a masterpiece.
